summary.text: Jeffrey Lipe is the Democratic candidate for the Utah House of Representatives, District 74, in the November 3, 2026 general election, facing incumbent Republican Neil Walter.
A retired U.S. Navy veteran and former defense contractor and federal employee, he said in a Ballotpedia survey that he wants to bring more transparency and balance to the legislature.

paragraphs.text: Lipe served in the U.S. Navy from 1978 to 1983 and is retired as of 2026, according to Ballotpedia.

In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he worked as a defense contractor for 15 years and then for 22 years as a Department of Defense federal employee, as a software engineer, systems engineer and software development manager.

He said he holds a bachelor's degree in computer science and a master's degree in software engineering, lived and worked in Virginia for 37 years, and moved to St. George, Utah, after retiring in 2020.
Lipe said he was a Republican for 44 years, an independent from about 2022 to 2025, and became a Democrat in 2025.

Among his stated priorities, he said he supports a living wage and organized labor, opposes approving major projects such as hyperscale data centers without public comment and review, and opposes mass surveillance systems such as Flock cameras.
He listed an endorsement from the Women's Democratic Club of Utah.
